one_liner: Telegram offers a free Bot API (bot token via @BotFather) and MTProto user API (api_id/hash); easy to build on, but only community MCP servers exist and there is no standard OAuth for API access.
auth_notes: Bot API uses a bot token from @BotFather (static secret). Telegram Login offers OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE, but it is for user sign-in to websites, not delegated API access to a user's account. MTProto user auth uses phone code, 2FA SRP and api_id/api_hash with session keys (OTHER). Gateway API uses a bearer token.
access_notes: Bot API and Telegram API (MTProto) are free. Bot token comes from @BotFather; api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org. Paid broadcasts above 30 msg/s cost Stars, and Gateway costs money, but the core API is free.
blocker_notes: Bot token model is per-bot, so each customer needs their own bot. User-account (MTProto) access has ToS and account-ban risks.

evidence.quote: To log in as a [bot](https://core.telegram.org/bots), follow [these instructions »](https://core.telegram.org/api/bots).
Our implementation follows the standard [Authorization Code Flow](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#CodeFlowAuth) with **PKCE** support.
You are welcome to use both APIs free of charge.
Go to ["API development tools"](https://my.telegram.org/apps) and fill out the form.
You communicate with this server via a simple HTTPS interface that offers a simplified version of the Telegram API.
